gen.instruction.text:
■ About this tool
Using the work folder prepared with asset_preparer, this tool mass-produces
lip-sync videos for every combination of character × prompt list.
It runs automatically from Phase1 (video generation via the Vidu API) through
Phase2 (mouth removal + background-transparent WebM conversion).

■ Workflow
1. Prompt Lists: prepare lists of motion prompts
   (up to five lists, A to E. Prepare only as many as you need)
2. Main: for each character, check the lists to use → Check Materials & Estimate → Start
   (e.g. if you check only List A, only the prompts in List A are used in order)
3. Queue Monitor: watch the execution status
4. Review Outputs: check background transparency and lip-sync motion
5. Regenerate: redo Phase2 only for videos where mouth removal failed

■ Outputs (inside each character folder)
{{job ID}}.webm … background-transparent video with the mouth removed
{{job ID}}.json … mouth position tracking data
original/ … original videos generated by Vidu (used for regeneration)

■ Interruption and resume
Progress is saved automatically to batch_state.json in the work folder.
Even if interrupted, you can pick up where you left off with "Resume Previous" on the Main page.

■ Cost warning
Phase1 consumes Vidu credits. Before starting, always check the number of
videos and the estimated credits with "Check Materials & Estimate".

gen.prompts.note:
You can set up five prompt lists, A to E (prepare only as many as you need). One row = one prompt = one video.
"Save" writes the list to prompt_lists/ and it is loaded automatically on the next launch.
Load from file: a JSON string array ["prompt1", "prompt2", ...] or a text file (one prompt per line; leading numbers and bullet marks are removed automatically).
Note: include wording that means "do not generate a mouth" (e.g. "Do not generate a mouth.") in every prompt. It reduces mouth-removal mistakes.
Note: background removal only keys out green (#00FF00). Always include wording that keeps the background green (e.g. "Keep the solid bright green background."), otherwise the background will not be removed.
gen.queue.note:
Phase1: generates videos via the Vidu API. Slots = the API's concurrency quota; jobs are submitted in parallel up to the limit.
Phase2: tracks each generated video with SAM3 and creates a mouth-removed, background-transparent WebM (one at a time due to GPU processing).
Jobs flow into Phase2 automatically as soon as their Phase1 finishes.
gen.regen.note:
This step redoes only the mouth removal (Phase2). It re-runs tracking → mouth removal → transparent WebM
from the source videos in original/ and overwrites the existing .webm / .json files. The Vidu API is not used, so no credits are consumed.
"Failed Only" = videos that did not finish due to a GPU error or interruption, plus videos whose mean
mouth-tracking confidence (mean_conf) was below 0.5. Failures caused by transient errors can be recovered here.
* Re-running the same video with the same settings yields nearly the same tracking quality. For videos that
keep failing on quality, regenerate them from Vidu instead. The "tolerance" and "smoothing" parameters on the
Settings page only adjust appearance (transparency / jitter).

gen.review.note:
This step is for checking the generated outputs.
Alpha Preview: verify that the background is properly transparent (transparent areas are shown in magenta; move between frames with the slider).
Character Player: actually animate the character and check the lip-sync (requires Node.js).
Delete videos with bad mouth movement using the "Delete" button on the left of the list (all related files are permanently deleted). The currently playing video (▶) cannot be deleted.
gen.settings.api_key_note: The API key is set in asset_preparer (page ⓪ Instructions). It cannot be changed here.
gen.settings.bg_note: Fixed green (#00FF00) + HSV edge correction. The tolerance can be adjusted.
gen.settings.resolution_fixed: 720p (fixed — to match the rescale in material preparation)
gen.settings.smooth_note:
Smooths out small jitters in the mouth position tracked in Phase2 with a low-pass filter.
Lower = smoother (may lag behind fast motion) / higher = more responsive (noise may remain). Usually 3.0 is fine.

prep.instruction.text:
■ About This Tool
From a single character image, this tool automatically generates a
lip-sync video, mouth sprites, and face info, and prepares a work folder
for video_generator (batch production).

■ Preparation (same order as the checklist below)
1. Required software: uv / Git / ffmpeg / Node.js.
   Running "Installer MotionPNGCreator for AG.bat" installs all of them
   automatically, but using the installer is NOT mandatory - it is just
   a convenience. You may install them manually via winget or from each
   official site instead (make sure they are on PATH; see "Manual setup"
   in the README).
2. SAM3 model: Get approval at https://huggingface.co/facebook/sam3,
   obtain sam3.pt, and place it in the Sam3/ folder (approval-gated,
   cannot be automated).
   An NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) is required. It may run on the CPU, but that is
   extremely slow, untested, and unsupported (AMD/Intel GPUs cannot be used).
   CUDA/cuDNN are installed automatically by uv sync.
3. Vidu API key: Obtain one and save it in the field below
   (video generation consumes credits).
4. Work folder: Create a folder anywhere on your PC and put the
   character images in it. This folder becomes the "work folder" used
   for this asset generation.
   * Even when generating only one character, create a folder and put
     the character image file inside it.
5. Character images: 1 character = 1 image. A closed mouth is recommended.
   The file name becomes the character name.
   Non-ASCII file names (such as Japanese) are fine.
   Characters not allowed in file names: \ / : * ? " < > | # %
   (no trailing space or dot, reserved names such as CON, or very long names)
   Keep the aspect ratio at 9:16.
   Watermarks from image-generation AI interfere with background removal,
   so they must be removed.
   Use images whose terms of use allow watermark removal
   (the "AI eraser" in Windows Photos editing can remove them easily).
   * Steps ①②⑥ overwrite the images in place. If you need the original
     images, keep a copy elsewhere before putting them in the work folder.

■ Workflow
Select the work folder and set the API key in ⓪. Once the checklist is
clear, proceed from ① in order; preparation is done when ⑦ is complete.

prep.tab1.note:
This step rescales the images to {w}x{h} to match the size of the generated videos (overwrites the files).
* Images that have already gone through ③ are not targeted.
* The original images are not kept. If you need them, keep a copy elsewhere beforehand.
prep.tab1.status_done: ✓ Done ({done}/{total} converted) — proceed to ② Background Color Replacement
prep.tab2.note:
This step repaints the background with green (#00FF00). The replacement color cannot be changed, because background removal in Step 2 only keys out green.
Left-click the preview to use the color at that spot as the reference color. Adjust the tolerance, check the selected area (shown in magenta) in the preview, then overwrite. Do this for every image.
* The original images are not kept. If you need them, keep a copy elsewhere beforehand.
prep.tab2.preview_frame: Preview (left-click to pick the reference color)
prep.tab3.log_mouth_suspicious: ⚠ {name}: the mouth detection looks wrong ({detail}). The image may have no mouth drawn. Re-run the detection on an image that has a mouth (closed is fine); otherwise the mouth erasure and mouth overlay will be misplaced during batch generation
prep.tab3.note:
This step uses SAM3 to extract the character's eye and mouth positions. Check in the preview that the eyes and mouth are captured correctly.
* Images directly under the work folder are automatically moved into a folder named after the character after detection.
prep.tab3.reason_done: Already processed (face_info.json exists). Delete face_info.json to re-detect.
prep.tab3.status_done: ✓ Done: {done}/{total} — proceed to ④ Vidu Video Generation
prep.tab4.estimate_unknown: Estimate: cost unknown for these settings
prep.tab4.note:
This step generates the videos with Vidu from which mouth images are extracted in ⑤.
This consumes credits. (One video per character; saved to: {{character name}}/{{character name}}.mp4)
prep.tab4.skip_existing: Skip characters that already have a video
prep.tab4.status_all_done: ✓ All characters generated — proceed to ⑤-1 Extract
prep.tab51.note:
This step analyzes the video with SAM3 and extracts mouth sprites.
From the candidates, pick one suitable sprite each for Open / Closed / Half, then press "Go to ⑤-2". Do this for every character.
prep.tab52.note:
This step finishes the mouth sprites extracted in ⑤-1.
During playback each sprite is drawn at its original size, centered on the tracked mouth position, so the preview here is exactly what you get (the checkerboard is the transparent area).
- Mask settings: the area cut out as the mouth. Use dilate/erode so the selection fits the mouth area as tightly as possible, and feather to soften the edge.
- Mouth position X/Y and size: where the mouth is drawn on the face (in px) and how large it is. Adjust when it looks misaligned or too big (making it too big crops the edges).
prep.tab6.edit_frame: Mouth Area (zoomed) — right-click: sample color / left-drag: paint
prep.tab6.note:
This step removes the mouth from the character image (generating video from a mouthless image makes mouth removal more stable).
Right-click to sample the color within the brush area → left-drag to paint over the mouth → save (overwrite). Do this for every character.
Saving overwrites the file; the original image is not kept. If you need it, keep a copy elsewhere beforehand.
If it does not come out well, remove the mouth with the "AI eraser" in Windows Photos editing and overwrite the file.
